source_credit: Robert Greene: The 48 Laws of Power (1998), The 33 Strategies of War (2006), The Art of Seduction (2001), The Laws of Human Nature (2018), Mastery (2012), The 50th Law (2009, with 50 Cent). Plain one-line maxims in our own words; only the ideas are Greene's, no passages are reproduced.

entries.text: Let your boss or a big customer feel smart. Do not show them up in public.
Be careful doing business with friends. A former rival with something to prove often works harder.
Do not announce plans before they are ready. Talk about them once they are done.
Say less than you planned. Short answers make people take you more seriously.
Protect your name every day. One bad job told around town costs more than any sale.
Give people a reason to remember you. Do one thing the others in town do not.
Hand off work others do well. Spend your time on what only you can do.
Make people want to come to you. A good offer works better than chasing.
Do not argue with a customer about the problem. Show them the worn part.
Spend less time with people who always complain. Their mood spreads to you and the crew.
Learn a skill nobody else near you has. Then people cannot do without you.
Be honest and generous early with a new customer. Trust built first makes the rest easier.
When you need a favor, show what they gain. Do not count on pity.
Keep track of what your rivals charge and offer. Check again every few months.
When you fix a problem, fix it all the way. A half fix comes back worse.
Do not jump at every small call. People value your time more when it is scarce.
Do not let others guess every move you make. Keep some room to change your plan.
Do not hide in the office. Stay out front where you can see what happens.
Before you push back on someone, learn who they are and what they can do.
Do not tie yourself to one supplier too soon. Keep other options open.
Let others feel smart when they explain things. You will learn more by listening.
When you are losing a fight, give in for now. Use the time to get stronger.
Find the one service that brings the most money. Put your best effort there.
Be polite with people who have power over you. Learn how they like things done.
Do not let others decide who you are. Choose the role you want and act it.
Stay away from shady deals, even small ones. Your name sticks to everything you touch.
People want something to believe in. Stand for something clear and stick to it.
Once you decide, commit fully. Halfway moves get pushback.
Before you start a big job, think through how it ends. Then begin.
Let customers see the clean result, not the struggle. Keep the stress behind the counter.
Give customers two or three clear options. Too many choices slow everyone down.
People buy peace of mind, not parts. Tell the truth and show the benefit.
Find out what each person cares about most. That is how you reach them.
Carry yourself with calm confidence. People treat you the way you treat yourself.
Do not rush in front of customers. Move steady and pick the right moment.
When you lose a deal, let it go. Do not waste energy complaining about it.
What people see beats what you say. Use photos and old parts to explain the work.
Keep strong opinions to yourself at work. Fit in when it costs you little.
When others lose their temper, stay calm. The calm person usually comes out ahead.
Be careful with free offers. Ask what they really cost before you say yes.
Build your own name. Do not just copy the last owner's way of doing things.
When there is trouble on the team, find who starts it. Deal with that one person.
Win people over instead of forcing them. Forced people push back later.
When someone treats you badly, repeat their words back calmly. Many will hear themselves and stop.
Change things a little at a time. Big changes all at once scare the crew.
Admit a small mistake now and then. Looking perfect makes people jealous.
When you hit your goal, stop and lock it in. Do not push past it.
Do not get stuck in one way of working. Change your plan when things change.
Know clearly what you are against. It makes what you stand for clearer.
Do not solve today's problem with last year's plan. Look at what is here now.
When things get hectic, slow your breathing. A calm boss keeps the crew steady.
Give yourself a real deadline. People work hardest when there is no way out.
Ask for input, then make the call yourself. Groups rarely decide well.
Give each worker a clear job and let them run it. Small teams move faster.
Tell the crew why the work matters. People work harder for a purpose than for pay.
Do not argue over every small thing. Save your energy for what matters.
When a rival makes a move, wait and watch. Respond where they left a gap.
Let people see you are ready and able. Most will not test you.
When you are not ready, step back and buy time. Rushed rivals wear themselves out.
Losing one sale is fine if it keeps the customer for years.
Before you act against a rival, learn all you can about them.
When the moment is right, move fast. Do not give others time to block you.
Set the pace in a deal. Make the other side respond to you.
Find the one thing your rival depends on most. Compete hard right there.
Break a big problem into small parts. Solve them one at a time.
If the direct way does not work, try a different approach.
Compete where you are strong and your rival is weak.
Shape how people see the problem first. The right action follows.
Watch for problems that start inside your own team. They hurt more than rivals do.
Watch for people who agree out loud but fight you quietly. Name it early.
Small problems spread fast. Fix the first one before it turns into many.
Pick partners for what they bring, not because you like them.
End things while they are still going well. People remember how you leave.
Make sure your deals help the other side too. Shared wins last longer.
In a negotiation, name your number first. It sets where the talk starts.
Make progress in small steps. Small changes are easier to get done than big ones.
Explain things in the customer's terms. Start from what they already know.
When a rival is hurting itself, stay out of the way. Just keep doing good work.
Guard the reasons people trust you, not just your prices. Lose that and little else holds.
If you take on a fight, commit fully. If not, stay out of it.
In a tough deal, do not reveal everything you think. Let them do the guessing.
For people who matter, stay in touch often and give them real time.
When a relationship is shaky, keep in touch but spend less on it.
When someone keeps crossing a line, see them less. Let the distance send the message.
When someone breaks a deal, respond right away. Say clearly what they did.
When you are not sure what is going on, do nothing yet. Watch first.
Put good partnerships in writing. Both sides should know what they give and get.
Gather the facts before you pick a plan.
When a relationship keeps hurting the business, end it cleanly. Do not drag it out.
See things as they are, not as you wish. Look at the real numbers.
Do not wait for someone else to fix your problems. Own them yourself.
When something goes wrong, ask what it lets you do next.
Keep moving even when unsure. Action opens choices that waiting never will.
Be firm when someone takes advantage of you. Stay soft and they will keep doing it.
Do the hard job first yourself. The crew follows what you do.
Work the floor with your crew. You learn more there than from any report.
There are no shortcuts to being great at something. Put in the hours.
Believe you can do a bit more than you think. Then try it.
Life is short. Do the important thing today, not someday.
When you start something new, learn how the best do it first.
Learn the basics deeply first. Your own ideas will come after.
Years of practice turn hard calls into quick, sure ones. Keep practicing.
Find someone who has done what you want to do. Their advice saves you years.
Trade advice with someone at your level. Hold each other to your goals.
Watch out for advisers who take more than they give. Drop them.
Teach a young worker well. What you put in pays back for years.
Not everyone has to be your teacher or your student. Some people are simply peers.
Stop copying others. Your own way may feel worse at first. Keep at it.
Look for the one fact that proves you wrong. It teaches more than many that agree.
Learn a job by doing it with your hands, not by reading about it.
Do work you are naturally drawn to. Forcing yourself into the wrong work shows.
Do not fight for a crowded market. Find a nearby niche where you set the standard.
Keep your main goal in sight. It tells you which details are worth your day.
Before you build something new, see if you can reuse what you already have.
Look at a problem from every side before you decide.
Fill your head with the problem, then step away. The answer often comes later.
Show up confident and present. People trust someone who is a little human, not perfect.
Give people your full attention when they talk. Focused attention earns trust fast.
Find out what each customer most needs. Then deliver that, honestly.
Be a little different so people remember you. Do not copy every other shop.
Be relaxed and real with people. Plain honesty puts customers at ease.
Do not chase people too hard. Give them room to come back on their own.
Make people feel heard. Remember their name and what they told you last time.
Have a clear mission and say it often. People follow someone who believes in something.
Do not overshare. People respect a leader who keeps some things private.
Some strict people miss having fun. Give them a little room to enjoy the work.
Some people still chase an old dream. Never sell them a promise you cannot keep.
Customers used to comfort notice every detail. Keep the waiting area clean and calm.
People who cut back on spending still want a treat. Offer good value, not pressure.
Some adults want to be taken care of. Be kind, but set clear limits.
If you love to help, watch for fake sob stories. Check before you give.
People who have seen it all respect plain honesty. Do not oversell them.
Do not treat any expert as perfect. Judge people by what they actually do.
Bosses can get lonely. Be careful of people who use that to get close.
When someone cannot take any criticism, keep talks short and stick to facts.
Watch for people who go quiet when you win. Do not share every success with them.
Judge people by what they deliver, not by how they talk about themselves.
If someone treats every comment as an attack, put feedback in writing and keep it short.
When someone uses guilt to get a yes, slow down. Decide later on your own.
When someone keeps forgetting or stalling on purpose, name it calmly and set a deadline.
Notice who leaves you tired every time you talk. Spend less time with them.
Be careful with people who keep telling you how good they are. Watch what they do.
Some people decide based on how things look. Know that before you make your pitch.
Some people only see flaws. Take the useful part of the criticism and ignore the rest.
Do not feed people who create a crisis every week. Stay calm and stick to facts.
Watch for people who are always the victim in their stories. Ask what part they played.
Do not trade next year for today. Cheap fixes now often cost more later.
When you feel upset, wait before you decide. Let the feeling pass first.
What people say they are and how they act often differ. Watch the actions.
Know your own bad habits. Hidden ones show up when you are stressed.
Use both your tough side and your gentle side. A good boss needs each one.
Know what you are aiming for. Daily choices get easier once the goal is clear.
Do not let the group lower your standards. Keep doing it right when others slack.
